+

+    ## Corporate Income Tax
+
+
+    Your business’s **net income** is subject to **corporate income tax**.
+
+
+    If your business loses money, the result is called a **deficit**. It
+
+    will not have to pay corporate income tax.
+
+
+    If your business makes money, the result is called a **profit**.
+
+    It will be taxed at a **fixed rate**.
+
+
+    The taxable income is determined when filing the **tax return**
+
+    (also called the income statement). Your accountant handles this.
+
+
+    Note: There are **two ways to pay yourself** from a business subject to
+
+    corporate income tax:
+      - You can pay yourself a salary as a business owner during
+      the year. This salary is deducted from the net income to calculate
+      your company’s taxable profit. However, this compensation is
+      added to your household’s taxable income when calculating income tax.
+      -
+      - You can also pay yourself dividends from the profits of
+      previous years. You will have to pay a flat tax on these dividends: this is
+      known as the “flat tax.”
+
+      In all cases, you will have to pay **social security contributions** on the
+      income you receive.
